security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD's cpu_switch (sys/riscv/riscv/swtch.S) saves only GPRs and FPU state but never saves/restores sstateen* CSRs. If the kernel writes per-process values to sstateen* to control which ISA extensions each process may access, a context switch leaks the previous process's sstateen bitmask into the next process, since the CSR file is hart-local and survives context switch.
security_spec.summary: sstateen* CSRs gate user-mode access to ISA extension state (FPU/vector/custom) but FreeBSD's context-switch path has no awareness of them; if populated per-process, bits bleed across context-switch boundaries, letting an unprivileged process access extensions the kernel meant to deny

findings.finding: cpu_switch saves GPRs (ra, sp, s0-s11) and conditionally saves/restores FPU state, but does not save/restore sstateen* CSRs. However, FreeBSD has zero smstateen implementation: no sstateen CSR reads/writes exist anywhere in the kernel (sys/riscv/), the PCB has no sstateen fields, bhyve has no sstateen virtualization, and the init/boot path does not configure smstateen. Since the kernel never writes per-process sstateen values, the violation precondition (per-process sstateen leakage) cannot be triggered. The CSR file persists across context switches, but its value is never modified from hardware reset default.

cpu_throw restores only GPRs and optionally FPU state. No sstateen* CSR restore. Same rationale as cpu_switch: FreeBSD does not implement smstateen, so no per-process sstateen state exists to leak or restore.
findings.snippet:
ENTRY(cpu_throw)
        /* Activate the new thread's pmap. */
        mv      s0, a1
        mv      a0, a1
        call    _C_LABEL(pmap_activate_sw)

findings.finding: PCB structure has no sstateen-related fields (only ra, sp, gp, tp, s[12], x[32][2], fcsr, fpflags, onfault). This is correct given the current lack of smstateen usage. If smstateen support is added, this struct must be extended with per-process sstateen0/1/2/3 save slots.
savectx saves GPRs and FPU state but no sstateen* CSRs. Consistent with the rest of the context-switch infrastructure — no smstateen support exists to require saving.
findings.snippet:
ENTRY(savectx)
        /* Store ra, sp and the callee-saved registers */
        sd      ra, (PCB_RA)(a0)
        sd      sp, (PCB_SP)(a0)
        sd      tp, (PCB_TP)(a0)
        sd      gp, (PCB_GP)(a0)

findings.finding: fork_trampoline restores sstatus and sepc (via csrw) and sscratch (for user trap handling) but no sstateen* CSRs. The fork path inherits whatever sstateen value the hardware has from reset — no per-process differentiation exists.
findings.snippet:
/* Restore sstatus */
        ld      t0, (TF_SSTATUS)(sp)
        ...
        csrw    sstatus, t0
        ...
        csrw    sepc, t0
